JUDGMENT

This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,000/- from respondents on account of damages sustained to petitioner's Zest- 110 Scooty, bearing No.KA-05-JY-8583 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are that, on 28- 08-2021 at about 9.10 p.m., petitioner was riding his Zest-110 Scooty, bearing No.KA-05-JY-8583 towards Uma Talkies on the extreme left side on Shankarpuram main road slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Shankarpuram Police Station, Bengaluru, at that time rider of Royal Enfield Classic-350 motorcycle, bearing No.KL-74-B-0282 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations dashed against petitioner's scooty.
Due to the impact, he fell 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 760/2022 down and scooty also badly damaged.
Immediately after the accident, scooty was towed to M/s. Skanda Motors, Hanumanthanagar, Bengaluru, wherein he got repaired the same by spending Rs.24,195/-.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.
3. Respondent No.1 remained absent and therefore, he was placed exparte.

3(a). Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle, bearing No.KL-74-B-0282, denied the other petition averments generally and contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.

As without prejudice, it contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident, the accident had occurred due to the sole negligence of petitioner himself who was riding the motorcycle without having valid driving licence and without wearing helmet and he was not possessed policy to his vehicle, complaint has been lodged after lapse of 2 months.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
4 (SCCH-16) MVC 760/2022 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that his Zest110 Scooty, bearing No.KA05JY 8583 sustained damages in the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on Sri T. Ramu vs Sri Vijeesh V on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6744902/
2 28082021 at about 9.10 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Royal Enfield Classic350 Motorcycle, bearing registration No.KL74B0282?

Issue No.1 : In the Negative Issue No.2 : In the Negative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following REASONS ISSUE No.1:
7.
Petitioner led his oral as well as documentary evidence.
Respondent No.1 remained exparte.
Respondent No.2 didn't lead evidence.
This is a summary proceedings, so, the sum and substance of 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 760/2022 the pleadings and evidences are only emphasized.
The petitioners need to prove this issue on preponderance of probability as test for proof is preponderance of probability herein.
The petition averments as well as the objections are summarized herein above in the brief facts of case and objections, so those are not repeated here in avoidance of repetition.
The damages are in dispute; the involvement of vehicles, incident, negligence, issuance of policy and its validity are not in dispute.

8. In proof of petition averments regarding damages the petitioner relied on police records viz. true copy of FIR, charge sheet, complaint, sketch, spot mahazar, job cards, service invoice and IMV reports which are marked in - Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
9.
The final report/charge sheet filed by V.V. Puram Traffic Police shows the negligence by the rider of Royal Enfield Classic 350 Motorcycle, bearing No.KL-74-B- 0282.
The brief facts of final report are extracted hereunder for better appreciation:

sentences.text: The spot mahazar and sketch depict the scene of occurrence.
The IMV reports show that there was no damages to the vehicles.
For better appreciation the particular part of report of Ex.P8 are extracted as follows; "KA-05-JY-8583 - a) MV

no damages found", and likewise, "KL-74-B-0282 - a)
MV no damages found".
The IMV reports are clear that there were no damages to both vehicles.

But,
the petitioner is claiming damages in view of Ex.P6, Ex.P7, Ex.P9 as well as Ex.P10.

When the motor vehicle inspection report from the competent authority is clear that there were no damages then the damages averred by the petitioner cannot be believed as the damages got repaired by the petitioner of his vehicle were not of out of the road traffic incident occurred on 28-08-2021 at about 9.10 p.m.
As per the final report there might be the incident but there could not be damages.
The final report is not clear regarding the damages.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 put suggestion regarding 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 760/2022 this in cross-examination of petitioner, for which the petitioner pleaded his ignorance.
The petitioner also pleaded his ignorance regarding non mentioning about the way of damages in Ex.P6 - job card.
It is admitted by the petitioner that no receipt on payment under Ex.P7 is produced.

11. Furthermore, it is significant to consider that the petitioner himself deposed orally that he did not give/lodge his first information statement/complaint, but Ex.P1 - FIR shows the petitioner himself informed the concerned police and he was the first informant/complainant, which allows court to doubt the case of the petitioner.

The admission by the petitioner is extracted here as follows for better appreciation;
"  ".
Thus, the averments are not corroborated.

12. Under the facts and circumstances of the case, it is found that though there was the incident involving the petitioner's vehicle and Royal Enfield Classic 350 motorcycle, bearing No.KL-74-B-0282, there were no damages to both vehicles.
13. Furthermore, it is pertinent to note here that petition averments are silent regarding the own damages claim from insurer of petitioner's vehicle.

Wherefore, for foregoing reasons it is not established that the petitioner's vehicle damaged in the road traffic accident occurred on 28-08-2021 at about 9.10 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of Royal Enfield Classic 350 motorcycle, bearing No.KL-74-B-0282.
Hence, this issue is answered negatively.

15.
In view of the discussions and the conclusiion arrived at on issue No.1 the pettioner is not entitled to the compensation from respondent No.2.
Hence, this issue stands answered Negatively.
